He played [[college basketball]] for the [[University of Kentucky]]. ==High school career== [[File:20130403 MCDAAG Dakari Johnson putback dunk (3).JPG|thumb|left|upright|Johnson at the [[2013 McDonald's All-American Boys Game]]]] Johnson first attended [[St. Patrick High School (New Jersey)|St. Patrick High School]] in [[Elizabeth, New Jersey]]. After the 2010–11 school year, when coach Kevin Boyle left for [[Montverde Academy]], Johnson followed his coach, where he had to sit out the 2011–12 season due to the transfer. Because of his excellent grades, Johnson decided to [[reclassification (education)|reclassify]], thus making the 2012–13 season his final and senior season at the high school level. He ended up averaging 17.0 points, 11.0 rebounds and 4.3 blocks per game as a senior.{{cite web|first=Roger|last=Rubin|title=NCAA Tournament: Brooklyn native Dakari Johnson showing NBA potential with Kentucky|url=http://www.nydailynews.com/sports/college/brooklyn-dakari-johnson-showing-cat-meow-article-1.1746471|access-date=April 4, 2014|work=NYDailyNews.com|date=April 4, 2014}} His senior year he garnered [[USA Today]] [[All-American]] Second-Team for his success. He subsequently earned selection to the [[2013 McDonald's All-American Boys Game]] and [[Jordan Brand Classic#2013|Jordan Brand Classic]]. Considered a five-star recruit by [[ESPN.com]], Johnson was ranked as the No. 2 center in the nation in 2013.{{cite web|title=Dakari Johnson Recruiting Profile|url=https://www.espn.com/college-sports/basketball/recruiting/player/_/id/119182/dakari-johnson|access-date=November 9, 2015|work=ESPN.com}} {{College Athlete Recruit Start|40=no|collapse=no|year=2013}} {{College Athlete Recruit Entry | recruit = Dakari Johnson | position = C | hometown = [[Brooklyn, New York|Brooklyn, NY]] | highschool = [[Montverde Academy]] | feet = 6 | inches = 10 | weight = 250 | 40 = | commitdate = January 5, 2013 | scout stars = 5 | rivals stars = 5 | 247 stars = 5 | espn stars = 5 | espn grade = 95 }} {{College Athlete Recruit End | rivals ref title = https://n.rivals.com/content/prospects/2013/dakari-johnson-1690 | scout ref title = https://247sports.com/Player/Dakari-Johnson-15257/ | espn ref title = http://www.espn.com/college-sports/basketball/recruiting/player/_/id/119182/dakari-johnson | rivals overall = 9 | scout overall = 10 | espn overall = 7 }} ==College career== As a freshman at [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball|Kentucky]] in 2013–14, Johnson spent the season backing up teammate [[Julius Randle]] and averaged 5.2 points and 3.9 rebounds in 39 games. As a sophomore the following season, he again played back-up, this time to freshman big man [[Karl-Anthony Towns]] and junior [[Willie Cauley-Stein]].{{cite web|first=Marc|last=Tracy|title=Ahead of the N.B.A. Draft, a Place for Dakari Johnson to Hone His Fine Art|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2015/06/25/sports/basketball/a-place-for-dakari-johnson-to-hone-his-fine-art-basketball.html|access-date=June 24, 2015|work=[[The New York Times]]|date=June 24, 2015}} He again appeared in 39 games in 2014–15 and averaged slightly higher numbers with 6.4 points and 4.6 rebounds per game.{{cite web|title=Dakari Johnson Stats|url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/players/dakari-johnson-1.html|access-date=November 9, 2015|work=Sports-Reference.com}} On April 9, 2015, Johnson declared for the [[NBA draft]], forgoing his final two years of college eligibility. He was joined alongside fellow Kentucky teammates in [[Aaron Harrison]], [[Andrew Harrison (basketball)|Andrew Harrison]], Karl-Anthony Towns, Willie Cauley-Stein, [[Trey Lyles]] and [[Devin Booker]].{{cite web|last1=Feldman|first1=Dan|title=Kentucky's Dakari Johnson declares for NBA draft|url=http://nba.nbcsports.com/2015/04/08/report-kentuckys-dakari-johnson-declares-for-nba-draft/|website=NBCsports|date=April 8, 2015 |access-date=April 10, 2016}} ==Professional career== ===Oklahoma City Blue (2015–2017)=== On June 25, 2015, Johnson was selected by the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]] with the 48th overall pick in the [[2015 NBA draft]].{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/thunder/news/thunder/draft_150625|title= Thunder Selects Cameron Payne and Dakari Johnson in the 2015 NBA Draft|date=June 26, 2015|work=NBA.com|access-date=June 26, 2015}} He later joined the Thunder for the [[2015 NBA Summer League]] where he averaged 7.6 points and 8.6 rebounds in five games.{{cite web|title=Summer League Player Profile – Dakari Johnson|url=http://www.nba.com/summerleague/2015/players/sl_dakari_johnson/|access-date=November 9, 2015|work=NBA.com|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150705012942/http://www.nba.com/summerleague/2015/players/sl_dakari_johnson|archive-date=July 5, 2015}} On November 3, 2015, he was acquired by the [[Oklahoma City Blue]] of the [[NBA Development League]], the affiliate team of the Thunder.{{cite web|title=Oklahoma City Blue Announces Training Camp Roster|url=http://oklahomacity.dleague.nba.com/news/201516_camproster/|access-date=November 9, 2015|work=NBA.com|date=November 3, 2015|archive-date=March 4, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304104544/http://oklahomacity.dleague.nba.com/news/201516_camproster/|url-status=dead}} On November 14, he made his professional debut in a 110–104 loss to the [[Austin Spurs]], recording 16 points, nine rebounds, one assist, one steal and one block in 33 minutes.{{cite web|url=http://dleague.nba.com/games/20151114/AUSOKL/|title=Oklahoma City Falls To Austin In Season Opener|date=November 14, 2015|work=NBA.com|access-date=January 31, 2016}} Johnson appeared in all 50 games for the Blue in 2015–16, averaging 12.3 points, 8.1 rebounds, 2.0 assists and 1.6 blocks per game.{{cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/dleague/players/j/johnsda06d.html|title=Dakari Johnson D-League Stats|work=Basketball-Reference.com|access-date=April 30, 2016}} He subsequently earned NBA D-League All-Rookie Team honors.{{cite web|url=http://dleague.nba.com/news/2015-16-all-nba-dleague-teams-release/|title=NBA Development League Announces 2015–16 All-NBA D-League Teams|work=NBA.com|date=April 29, 2016|access-date=April 30, 2016|archive-date=September 4, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160904054918/http://dleague.nba.com/news/2015-16-all-nba-dleague-teams-release/|url-status=dead}} Johnson returned to the Blue for the 2016–17 season, and on February 6, 2017, he was named in the Western Conference All-Star team for the 2017 NBA D-League All-Star Game.{{cite web|url=http://dleague.nba.com/news/2017-nba-development-league-all-star-game-rosters/|title=Rosters for 2017 NBA Development League All-Star Game Presented By Kumho Tire|work=NBA.com|date=February 6, 2017|access-date=February 7, 2017}} ===Oklahoma City Thunder (2017–2018)=== [[File:Dakari Johnson - 2018 NBA Summer League.png|thumb|left|150px|Johnson at the [[2018 NBA Summer League]].]] On July 22, 2017, Johnson signed with the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]].{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/article/2017/07/22/oklahoma-city-thunder-sign-center-dakari-johnson#/|title=Oklahoma City Thunder sign center Dakari Johnson|work=NBA.com|date=July 22, 2017|access-date=July 22, 2017}} He scored four points in his NBA debut on October 19, 2017, in the Thunder's 105–84 win over the [[New York Knicks]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400974441|title=Thunder top Knicks 105–84 in OKC debuts for George, Anthony|work=ESPN.com|date=October 19, 2017|access-date=October 20, 2017}} During his only season with the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]], he started six games for the team where he replaced [[Steven Adams]]. As the starting center for the team they went 5–1 in those games. Johnson was a plus-26 in point differential in those six games, including a plus-26 in rout to a victory against the [[Los Angeles Clippers]] when Johnson held his own against [[DeAndre Jordan]]. Johnson's averages for those six games were 15 minutes, 5.2 points, 2.2 rebounds, 0.3 turnovers, 64.7 percent shooting and 60 percent foul shooting.{{cite web|url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/94608660/johnsons-nba-education-continues/|title=Johnson's NBA education continues|author=Brett Dawson|work=The Daily Oklahoman|date=May 21, 2018|page=14|access-date=December 18, 2020}} On July 20, 2018, Johnson was traded to the [[Orlando Magic]] in exchange for [[Rodney Purvis]]. Cash considerations were also sent to the Magic.{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/thunder/news/purvis-180720|title=Thunder Acquires Rodney Purvis|work=NBA.com|date=July 20, 2018|access-date=July 21, 2018}} On July 23, 2018, Johnson and the draft rights to [[Tyler Harvey (basketball)|Tyler Harvey]] were traded to the [[Memphis Grizzlies]] in exchange for [[Jarell Martin]] and cash considerations.{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/grizzlies/news/memphis-grizzlies-complete-trade-with-orlando-magic-180723|title=Memphis Grizzlies complete trade with Orlando Magic|work=NBA.com|date=July 23, 2018|access-date=July 23, 2018}} On August 31, 2018, Johnson was waived by the [[Memphis Grizzlies]].{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/grizzlies/news/memphis-grizzlies-waive-dakari-johnson-180831|title=Memphis Grizzlies waive Dakari Johnson|work=NBA.com|date=August 31, 2018|access-date=August 31, 2018}} .0 || .0 {{S-end}} ==Personal life== Dakari comes from a basketball family in Brooklyn, New York, where he is a third-generation basketball player. His family's basketball legacy started with his grandfather Leslie R. Campbell, best known as [[Jitu Weusi]], who played college basketball at [[LIU Brooklyn Blackbirds men's basketball|Long Island University]]. His mother Makini Campbell also played at [[LIU Brooklyn Blackbirds women's basketball|Long Island University]], and his uncle Kojo Campbell played basketball at [[Stony Brook Seawolves men's basketball|Stony Brook University]].{{Cite news|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2018/01/27/sports/basketball/thunder-dakari-johnson.html|title=A Brooklyn Family's Journey Finally Reaches the N.B.A.|first=Amos|last=Barshad|work=The New York Times |date=January 27, 2018|via=NYTimes.com}} His brother [[Kamani Johnson]] played basketball at [[Little Rock Trojans men's basketball|Arkansas-Little Rock]] before transferring to [[Arkansas Razorbacks men's basketball|Arkansas]].{{Cite web|url=https://lrtrojans.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/kamani-johnson/4523|title=Kamani Johnson – 2019–20 – Men's Basketball|website=Little Rock Athletics}}{{cite web |last1=Cawood |first1=Mike |title=Kamani Johnson Signs With Arkansas |url=https://arkansasrazorbacks.com/kamani-johnson-signs-with-arkansas/ |website=ArkansasRazorbacks.com |date=October 26, 2020 |publisher=University of Arkansas Athletics |access-date=5 December 2020}} His cousin Michael Murray played college basketball at [[Coppin State Eagles men's basketball|Coppin State University]], where he was selected all-[[Mid-Eastern Athletic Conference|MEAC]] his senior year. Most recently, Michael played professionally in Spain. Dakari is married to his long-term girlfriend Mercedes Johnson from Las Vegas, Nevada, who has been by his side since 2015.
